name: Northern Ireland
summary_text: Northern Ireland carries three sub-national negatives absent elsewhere in the UK: Education Minister Paul Givan ordered the 2019 transgender-pupils guidance withdrawn from the Education Authority website in September 2025 after the FWS ruling, calling it "unlawful and flawed" and a product of "activist campaigns"; the Justice Minister's attempt to include transgender people as a protected group in hate-crime sentencing reform was stalled (reported DUP obstruction); and the Rainbow Project records a pattern of paramilitary-flavoured anti-LGB&T violence including a pipe bomb thrown through the home of a trans woman in Derry/Londonderry described by PSNI as a "sectarian hate crime," a 2019 Belfast city-centre assault hospitalising a gay man, and an average of ~290 anti-LGB&T incidents per year (2013–2017) with rising transgender-identity strand counts to September 2025. Counter-balancing: PSNI/NISRA track a separate "transgender identity" category (unlike England and Wales), evidencing institutional recognition; the Health Minister publicly defended gender-identity service funding (£800k+ uplift) against DUP/TUV criticism, showing the executive is split rather than uniformly hostile. No criminal ban on expression or police-enforced facility prohibition exists — the risk mechanism mirrors the national EHRC code (service refusal by staff) plus street-level violence.

sources.title: Transgender pupils: Guidance for schools removed from website
sources.claim_summary: BBC News NI (8 September 2025): the Education Authority's 2019 guidance on supporting transgender pupils is withdrawn from its website after the UK Supreme Court biological-sex ruling; Education Minister Paul Givan requested the withdrawal, said the guidance did not reflect departmental policy and was inconsistent with NI law, and called it a product of activist campaigns; opposition parties press for reinstatement and disclosure of the legal advice.

sources.title: DUP accused of stalling trans hate crime protections
sources.claim_summary: BBC: the Justice Minister's attempt to add transgender people as a protected group in Northern Ireland's hate-crime sentencing reform is being stalled, with the DUP reported to be blocking the measure.

sources.title: Exploding pipe bomb thrown through transgender woman's window while she watched TV in 'hate crime' attack - The Mirror
sources.claim_summary: Daily Mirror: an exploding pipe bomb was thrown through the window of the home of Rachael Keys, a 27-year-old trans woman, in the Lincoln Court area of Derry/Londonderry while she watched television; PSNI treated it as a hate crime with sectarian framing and she was forced to move out.

sources.title: Anti LGB&T Hate Crimes in Northern Ireland - The Rainbow Project
sources.claim_summary: Rainbow Project Northern Ireland hate-crime monitoring page: an average of about 290 reported anti-LGB&T incidents and crimes per year (2013–2017), reporting stagnant, and quarterly series running back to 2004/05 including a separate transgender-identity strand.

sources.title: Mike Nesbitt defends funding boost for gender identity services
sources.claim_summary: BBC: the Health Minister publicly defends an uplift of more than £800k for gender-identity health services against DUP/TUV criticism, evidencing a divided executive rather than uniform hostility.
